articles.title: Jon Jones finally remembers longtime “frenemy” Daniel Cormier after struggling through hilarious pizza challenge
articles.summary: Jon Jones has once again brought Daniel Cormier into the spotlight, but this time in a much lighter way.
articles.body: Jon Jones has once again brought Daniel Cormier into the spotlight, but this time in a much lighter way. The former UFC champion appeared to remember his longtime rival while taking part in a pizza challenge. After only a few bites, Jones joked that he needed help from Cormier to get through the challenge.Jones and Cormier shared one of the fiercest rivalries in UFC history. Their rivalry featured heated exchanges, a famous media-day brawl and two championship fights. While their relationship has become more cordial over the years, Cormier has made it clear that the two are not friends. Jones’ latest comment, however, showed that their rivalry can still produce plenty of laughs.Jon Jones calls on Daniel Cormier for help during pizza challengeDuring a recent pizza challenge, Jon Jones appeared to struggle after eating only a few bites. The moment prompted him to jokingly call on the man who was once his biggest rival inside the UFC.“I have never wanted to see Daniel Cormier more than I want to see him right now. Tag in brother”, he said.The comment became a funny reminder of one of the most famous rivalries in MMA history. Jones and Cormier spent years trading verbal shots and building intense animosity before finally settling their differences inside the Octagon.Their first fight took place at UFC 182 in January 2015. Jones entered the bout as the UFC light heavyweight champion and defeated Cormier by unanimous decision. The fight was the culmination of years of tension between the two fighters.The rivalry became even more heated before their first meeting. In 2014, Jones and Cormier were involved in a wild confrontation during a UFC 178 media event. The two fighters got into a physical altercation during their face-off, with the incident spilling from the stage into the lobby.They eventually met again at UFC 214 in July 2017. Jones stopped Cormier with a third-round head kick and punches. However, the result was later overturned to a No Contest after Jones tested positive for turinabol. Jones was stripped of the title, while Cormier was reinstated as champion.Despite the bitter history, their relationship has changed over time. The two have been able to appear together professionally and interact without the same level of hostility that defined their rivalry during their fighting careers.However, Cormier has previously explained that he does not consider Jones a friend. Their history remains too complicated, particularly because of the controversies surrounding Jones’ drug-testing history.Cormier retired from MMA in 2020 after completing his trilogy with Stipe Miocic. Jones later moved to heavyweight and became the UFC heavyweight champion.Their competitive careers have taken them in different directions. Yet moments like Jones’ pizza challenge comment show that Cormier remains a familiar name in his mind. articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Tickets priced up to £13,000 for all-British showdown sell out in one hour
articles.summary: Tickets for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's fight at Cardiff's Principality Stadium sells out in just one hour.
articles.body:
Tickets for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's fight at Cardiff's Principality Stadium have sold out in just one hour.

Fury and Joshua will meet on a bill that begins on 11 December but they are not expected to fight until the early hours of 12 December.

The highest-priced tickets were available at £13,128, including booking fees, with the lowest at £88.50.

The all-British heavyweight contest, which will be broadcast globally on Netflix, was announced in September and around 80,000 tickets went on sale at 12:00 BST on Friday.

Just minutes after the tickets went on sale more than 500,000 people were waiting in the online queue.

Tickets quickly began emerging on resale websites, with ringside VIP seats being advertised for £73,645, while upper tier seats were available for £425.

Ringwalks are expected to start around 01:00 GMT on Saturday 12 December, following a short live music performance, and the stadium will remain open until 03:30.

The event is being promoted as a collaboration between Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and UFC chief Dana White.

Organisers are yet to confirm any of the undercard fights.

Joshua, 36, and Fury, 38 - both former two-time world champions - signed contracts for the bout earlier this year, but the date and venue had yet to be confirmed.

London's Wembley Stadium and New York's Madison Square Garden were the frontrunners to stage the fight, but both presented issues before Cardiff emerged as an alternative.

The Principality Stadium has hosted late-night boxing before, including Joe Calzaghe's fight with Mikkel Kessler in November 2007, which began at 01:00 GMT.

Ricky Hatton's victory over Kostya Tszyu at Manchester's MEN Arena in 2005 began at about 02:00 local time, allowing US broadcaster Showtime to show the fight on Saturday evening.

Just 11 days ago, there was uncertainty over whether the fight would even take place due to a dispute over the role of UFC chief White in the promotion of the event.

Broadcaster Netflix said Alalshikh's The Ring and White would collaborate to promote the event, but Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn said his fighter's contract prevented White from having a promotional role.

The British rivals finally met at a news conference on 30 September to begin the build-up to one of the most anticipated fights in British history.

Fury and Joshua are reported to be sharing a purse worth close to $200m (£151m)

articles.title: Who is Plinio Cruz? All about Alex Pereira’s coach set to make boxing debut against Gary Olive
articles.summary: Plinio Cruz is best known as the head coach and translator of UFC superstar Alex Pereira.
articles.body: Plinio Cruz is best known as the head coach and translator of UFC superstar Alex Pereira. The Brazilian-American mixed martial arts coach has played an important role in Pereira’s rise to the top of the sport. He has also worked with several other fighters, including former UFC light heavyweight champion Glover Teixeira. Cruz has built a reputation for his coaching skills, martial arts knowledge, and close relationship with Pereira.Cruz is now preparing for a new challenge outside mixed martial arts. He is set to make his boxing debut against Gary Olive at a Misfits Boxing event in London on October 10, 2026. The bout was arranged after original opponent Chase DeMoor withdrew because of an eye injury.Who is Plinio CruzPlinio Cruz has established himself as a respected coach in the mixed martial arts community. He serves as the head coach at Cruz Mixed Martial Arts, also known as Cruz MMA. His work involves preparing fighters for competition and helping them develop their skills inside the cage.Cruz is particularly recognised for his partnership with Alex Pereira. He has coached the Brazilian star throughout his rise in combat sports and has also helped him communicate with English-speaking audiences. His role as Pereira’s translator has made him a familiar face to UFC fans.The coach has also worked with Glover Teixeira, a former UFC light heavyweight champion. In addition, he has trained rising heavyweight fighter King Edokpolo. His experience working with fighters at different stages of their careers has helped establish his reputation in the sport.Cruz’s achievements have also received recognition at the World MMA Awards. He won the Coach of the Year award at the 16th edition of the ceremony, highlighting his contribution to the sport.Beyond coaching, Cruz has a background as a professional mixed martial artist. He competed in the heavyweight division and reportedly finished his professional career with an 8-9 record. He is also a former Cage Fury Fighting Championships heavyweight champion and competed under promotions such as Bellator and M-1 Global.Cruz has extensive martial arts experience. He holds a third-degree black belt in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu and a second-degree black belt in judo. These qualifications reflect his experience in grappling and other traditional martial arts disciplines.Cruz is now stepping into the boxing ring for the first time as a competitor. He was initially scheduled to face Chase DeMoor, the Misfits Boxing heavyweight champion, on October 10 at the Copper Box Arena in London. However, DeMoor withdrew after suffering an eye injury.The promotion subsequently announced that Gary Olive, DeMoor’s coach, would replace him. The contest was described as a “Battle of the Coaches.”Cruz’s boxing debut gives the experienced MMA coach an opportunity to test himself in a different combat sport. articles.title: La campeona olímpica y mujer hiperandrógina Imane Khelif retoma su paso al profesionalismo
articles.standfirst: Debutará por fin en diciembre en París tras suspenderse su debut en abril por una lesión
articles.summary: Debutará por fin en diciembre en París tras suspenderse su debut en abril por una lesión
articles.body: La boxeadora argelina Imane Khelif, posiblemente el oro olímpico más polémico de París 2024 por su condición de mujer hiperandrógina, ha retomado su idea de pasarse al profesionalismo tras un primer intento frustado por una lesión. La idea es que debute en diciembre en París frente a un rival aún por determinar. Así lo ha revelado el diario L'Equipe en un artículo en el que relata que en esta nueva aventura va de la mano del promotor Yacin Berrabah. El combate sería el 11 de diciembre en el Dôme de París o el 17 en el Clichy Hall (Hauts-de-Seine), aunque hasta el 5 de noviembre no se desvelarán más detalles. La campeona olímpica en la categoría de -66 kg firmó inicialmente con Brahim Asloum, el hombre que derrotó a Rafael Lozano en la final olímpica del peso minimosca (-48 kilos) en Sidney 2000, para convertirse en profesional e iba a debutar el 23 de abril en la Salle Wagram de París, pero una lesión en el hombro obligó a cancelar este combate. Tras este intento frustrado, la argelina ha puesto su carrera en manos de Yacin Berrabah, un experimentado promotor que organiza tanto veladas de boxeo como de kickboxing. "El director ejecutivo de su principal patrocinador, la marca argelina de cosméticos Belnco, me contactó para conseguirle una pelea", explicó Berrabah a L'Equipe. "Conocí a Imane y tengo un acuerdo con ella para sus tres primeras peleas. Estoy buscando una televisión (su pelea podría transmitirse por Twitch) y patrocinadores, pero no quiero interponerme en su camino, y si algún promotor extranjero importante está interesado en representarla, será bienvenido", añadió este ex campeón del mundo de kickboxing. Imane Khelif, de 26 años, sueña con defender su oro olímpico en Los Ángeles 2028 pero de momento no cuenta con el beneplácito de World Boxing, organismo que asumió provisionalmente la gestión del boxeo olímpico y que ya le impidió participar en el Mundial de septiembre de 2025 en Liverpool tras negarse a someterse a las pruebas genéticas de sexo para verificar la ausencia del gen SRY (típico del cromosoma Y). La argelina ha declarado que no se niega a pasar pruebas genéticas siempre que sean bajo el amparo del Comité Olímpico Internacional y ha presentando un recurso ante el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) para recuperar sus derechos deportivos.

articles.title: Anthony Cacace vs Nick Ball: Vasiliy Lomachenko interest not a distraction for world champion
articles.summary: WBA super-featherweight champion Anthony Cacace is not prepared to allow suggestions of a showdown with Vasiliy Lomachenko distract him as he prepares to take on Nick Ball.
articles.body:
WBA super-featherweight champion Anthony Cacace is not prepared to allow suggestions of a showdown with Vasiliy Lomachenko distract him as he prepares to take on Nick Ball.

The 37-year-old makes his maiden defence of the title against Liverpool's former WBA featherweight champion Ball at the recently renamed O2 Belfast on Saturday, 19 December.

The WBA has already indicated the winner must face Russia's Elnur Samedov next, but the returning Lomachenko is reported to be keen too, according to ESPN's Brian Custer. , external

Should that come to pass, it would represent the realisation of a dream for Cacace, but his immediate gaze remains firmly fixed on Ball.

"I'm not really thinking about that just now, I just kind of want to focus fully on Nick Ball and this fight coming up," he insisted.

"I woke up to them type of things [Lomachenko interest] going to myself, 'what?'. To see that type of stuff blows my mind but it's one of those things and I'm just super grateful for it all.

"I remember putting a tweet out in 2012 calling out Lomachenko, so if that fight ever materialises, I'll get that tweet sorted."

The last time Cacace boxed in the arena was in 2023, out-pointing Damian Wrzesinski over 12 rounds on the undercard of Luis Alberto Lopez's defeat of Michael Conlan in an IBF featherweight title defence.

Sandwiched between those two bouts was a victory for Ball over Ludumo Lamati, a fight that ended in worrying scenes with the South African suffering a stroke in the ring when stopped in the final round, but has since made a full recovery.

The Liverpudlian "didn't even know that" he and Cacace shared that undercard but was more than happy to return to Belfast for this opportunity.

Three successful defences would follow, but in February of this year, it all unravelled in the final round against Brandon Figueroa when he was dropped twice and then stopped, suffering his first career loss in his 25th professional bout.

"It was a good fight, back and forth for 12 rounds and he caught me with a good shot in the last round," Ball reflected.

"He threw an overhand left counter as I was throwing, so that's what happened. It's boxing, it's part of the game."

A bundle of aggression, Ball brings a relentless style but will concede considerable height and reach advantages to Cacace in what his his first step up into the super-featherweight division with the opportunity to become a two-weight champion "something special".

The move up was prompted by this opportunity alone, but feels he will be "stronger, more comfortable" and is not concerned about fighting a much bigger man.

"All fights are challenging," he countered.

"The reach and the size advantage [for opponents], I've been doing that my whole career, so that's nothing new to me."

'Dream come true' for Cacace to defend at home

In his 26-fight career, Cacace has boxed in his native Belfast on just five occasions, so to headline in his home city for the first time in a world title defence is "a dream come true".

He has been riding the crest of a wave since winning his first world title in 2024 when he stopped Joe Cordina for the IBF version in Saudi Arabia - and there has been no looking back.

Wins over Josh Warrington and Leigh Wood - which came after vacating the title - would set him up for a shot at then WBA-holder James 'Jazza' Dickens earlier this year and it proved another night of glory for a man whose career had previously been confined to the shadows.

"I always wanted to come back and have one big show," he said. "It's a dream come true. I never believed I'd be in this situation, but here I am.

"I'm just expecting the usual Nick Ball, [he'll] come forward with aggression.

"I feel like I can do it all. I can deal with him and deal with those styles for 20-plus years, so it's just going to be another fight, another good fight and hopefully a good show for Belfast."

articles.title: Volkanovski: "Solo quiero tener éxito por el bien de mi familia"
articles.standfirst: El campeón de peso pluma ha vuelto a dar ejemplo de su sencillez con unas sorprendentes declaraciones
articles.summary: El campeón de peso pluma ha vuelto a dar ejemplo de su sencillez con unas sorprendentes declaraciones
articles.body: Alexander Volkanovski es una de las mayores leyendas que han pasado por la UFC. El peleador australiano es considerado el GOAT de peso pluma, donde solo ha perdido con Ilia Topuria, y tiene en su historial victorias ante algunos de los nombres más importantes de la historia de la compañía. Sin embargo, en unas recientes declaraciones ha dado ejemplo de su sencillez afirmando que lo único que le importa de su fama y sus logros es el bien de su familia. Ni las tres victorias ante Max Holloway, ni ante José Aldo, o su histórica pelea ante Islam Makhachev en su país... A 'The Great' lo único que le preocupa es que esa grandeza se traduzca en bienestar para los suyos. Volk nunca ha sido una persona pretenciosa ni con mucho ego, y su humildad le ha llevado a ser uno de los peleadores más queridos de la UFC. Escuchando estas declaraciones uno entiende el por qué. "No me importa el legado, los cinturones ni nada de eso. Solo quiero tener éxito por mi familia", afirmó en una entrevista con 'Main Event TV'. Hace no tanto, el peleador australiano reconoció que necesitaba pelear de continuo para evitar caer en un pozo sin fondo por culpa de problemas de salud mental. Sin embargo, ha encontrado en su familia el apoyo para salir de esa situación y darlo todo por ellos. El próximo 24 de octubre, Volkanovski se enfrentará a Movsar Evloev para intentar defender el cinturón de peso pluma en el combate estelar del UFC 333 de Abu Dhabi. A sus 38 años no le quedan muchas más balas en la recámara, pero en sus últimas apariciones ha demostrado que todavía tiene lo suficiente para mantener a raya a las nuevas generaciones. Desde que Topuria subió a peso ligero, 'The Great' no ha encontrado rival alguno, aunque hay algunos nombres que vienen pisando fuerte como Jean Silva o Kevin Vallejos. Seguramente su siguiente derrota -si acaso pierde- signifique su adiós definitivo de la UFC, pero su legado será imborrable. Ya no solo sus victorias, sino el ejemplo que ha dado al mundo de reponerse ante las adversidades, nunca rendirse y poner buena cara por mucho que la situación no invite a ello. Seguramente se vaya por la puerta de atrás, sin hacer ruido, tal y como llegó. Por él hablarán los recuerdos que deja atrás, y los que todavía tiene pendientes.

articles.title: Commentator Katie Zacharia picked as new White House press secretary
articles.summary: The conservative commentator currently works as a communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group.
articles.body:
Donald Trump has chosen conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary.

Zacharia, who currently works for Trump Media & Technology Group, will become the US president's sixth chief spokesperson across his two administrations. She previously had a brief stint as a spokeswoman at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Trump called Zacharia "loyal" and "a devoted fan and member of MAGA" in a social media post on Friday, referring to his Make America Great Again movement, adding that she had "an unblemished record of support".

Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who left the White House in August, has reportedly taken a job with Fox News.

"She was previously involved in my Campaigns, assisting in key Swing States, where we won 7 out of 7," Trump wrote on Truth Social of Zacharia.

"I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration."

Zacharia thanked him in a post on X, writing: "Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime."

She said Trump had "shown America that we can be great again, and he works to effectuate that greatness every single day".

She said she looked forward "to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out".

The 42-year-old political strategist is a frequent fixture on conservative Newsmax and Fox News, and has been active in Republican politics for most of her adult life, having worked as an intern for the Republican National Committee and for the White House Office of Political Affairs during the Bush administration in 2006.

Since June, she has been a senior communications adviser for Trump's media company and Truth Social platform, according to her LinkedIn profile. She worked in Homeland Security from February to March this year.

While she was only briefly in government at DHS - which the mother of four later said she left because of the strain of travel between California and Washington on her family - she has long been a ferocious defender of President Trump and his administration's policies.

In a June interview with the BBC , for example, she dismissed criticism of Trump's controversial use of the White House to host a televised UFC fight, saying the principles of the UFC "are the kind of principles that founded our Constitutional Republic".

"It's about not giving up the fight until the bitter end," she said. "I think there's no better summation of the American ethos than a good UFC fight."

Earlier this year, Zacharia wrote an op-ed in the New York Post about an incident in which she was asked to stop wearing a "Make America Great Again" hat to her local gym.

"I responded that I would never take my Trump hat off to appease the left," she wrote. "This is raw, unfiltered intolerance. Freedom of speech doesn't evaporate at the gym door."

Justin Buchler, a political science professor at Case Western Reserve University in Ohio, told the BBC that Trump's appointments during his second term have been "based on personal affiliation and loyalty".

"He values loyalty first and foremost," Buchler told the BBC.

A lawyer educated at Pepperdine University in California, Zacharia also served as general counsel for Fix California, a conservative non-profit started by Trump ally - and current Special Presidential Envoy for Special Missions - Ric Grenell.

In 2011, she spent nearly two years clerking at a law firm in Beijing, China.

Trump says White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave post

The complex job of press secretary goes beyond the briefing room podium to include managing contentious relationships with the press, coordinating with other parts of the White House, and providing media advice to the president. The secretary also oversees an office that receives a significant amount of inquiries and requests on a daily basis.

Yanna Krupnikov, a political scientist and professor of communication and media at the University of Michigan, said the selection of Zacharia "speaks to a blurring of the lines between different media types".

Politicians nowadays need to communicate not only to various news outlets but with people in a social media context, she said.

"I think the goal is not as much speaking to the media and journalists, but making sure that particular, very specific sound-bytes and messages get to ordinary people," Krupnikov told the BBC.

When Leavitt left the role, Trump called her one of his "most trusted aides", which sets a high bar for her replacement. Leavitt left because she said she wanted to spend more time with her family.

articles.title: Exclusive-Erik Prince's forces suffer battlefield loss in Congo, former UFC fighter among wounded, sources say
articles.summary: By Jessica Donati DAKAR, Oct 9 (Reuters) - Blackwater founder Erik Prince's forces suffered a major battlefield loss in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo...
articles.body:
DAKAR, Oct 9 (Reuters) - Blackwater founder Erik Prince's forces suffered a major battlefield loss in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in mid-September when enemy forces ambushed them, killing and wounding at least 20 people, including a popular former UFC fighter, sources close to the government and his company said.

The frontline clash ‌shows how Prince, an ally and supporter of US President Donald Trump, has taken on an expanded role in Congo through his company Vectus Global. The company, which ‌also operates in Haiti and other parts of Africa, provides consulting and security services and previously helped Congo's army secure the city of Uvira in South Kivu against Rwanda-backed rebels who control swathes of the east.

A veteran special operator reported on ​his podcast earlier this week that former US Green Beret and Ultimate Fighting Championship contestant Tim Kennedy was injured in Congo. The involvement of Prince's forces and the number of casualties have not previously been reported.

The attack in South Kivu on September 17 left about 20 dead and wounded, two sources working with Congo's government said. The dead included at least seven Congolese and a former member of New Zealand's Special Forces, while the wounded included Kennedy and another foreign contractor, the sources said.

A Vectus Global representative declined to comment. The company has not previously suffered casualties in Congo, a source with direct ‌knowledge of the operation said.

One of the sources who works for ⁠Congo's government said that Rwandan forces backing the M23 rebels may have surprised them by tracking a drone used for surveillance operations to their location.

Spokespeople for the Congolese and Rwandan governments and for the M23 did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Kennedy, the former mixed martial arts fighter, survived the attack ⁠with three gunshot wounds to the leg, three sources said, and is being treated at the Walter Reed National Military Medical Center in the suburbs of Washington.

Kennedy has a popular podcast channel and millions of followers on social media. Trump is a fan of UFC, hosting fights at the White House this year.

The US State Department and Walter Reed declined to comment. Kennedy's parents did not respond to requests for comment.

A ​Congolese ​security source, who said some 20 people were wounded and killed in the attack, added that villagers were likely ​among the casualties as well. Reuters spoke to at least 10 sources ‌either with direct knowledge of the attack or briefed on the outcome.

PRINCE TOOK EXPANDED ROLE IN CONGO'S CONFLICT

Prince's initial mandate in Congo was to secure and improve revenue collection from the country's vast mineral reserves, which have been plundered for decades, fuelling relentless conflict in the east.

But in January and early February, his forces deployed to Uvira after Washington helped broker a deal for Rwandan-backed rebels to withdraw from the strategic town.

The size of Prince's forces in Congo is unclear.

One of the sources with direct knowledge of the attack said the Vectus team was travelling between locations when the ambush took place and its sophistication suggested Rwandan forces were involved.

"It reinforces the need for DRC sovereignty to be restored. It's an incredibly dangerous place right now," the source said.

Two ‌other sources said the ambush was carried out by the Rwandan military.

Prince is the founder of now-defunct ​private military firm Blackwater, some of whose members were pardoned in 2020 for killing Iraqi civilians.

The State Department has ​said it does not have any contracts with Prince in Congo, though US officials have ​said they plan to work more closely with Vectus Global in Haiti.

The deal for Rwandan-backed rebels to withdraw from Uvira was part of wider agreements brokered ‌by the Trump administration to try to end the conflict in eastern ​Congo.

Kennedy, a father of four, has posted ​his views on politics, culture, fitness and more on social media. He also runs a popular YouTube podcast in which he interviews UFC fighters, veterans, cultural disruptors and others.

He has often posted about his family, including four young children. In late August, he posted about having "incredible conversations about what being a man means and what sacrifice really looks like" ​with his son. He did not disclose details about his upcoming ‌trip to Congo.

The United Nations and Western powers say Rwanda backs M23, even exercising command and control over the group. Rwanda denies this. Fighting in the decades-long ​conflict flared early last year, with M23 fighters making rapid gains in the east, which is rich in tantalum, gold, lithium and other minerals.

(Additional reporting by Clement ​Bonnerot in Dakar and David Lewis in London; Writing by Jessica Donati; Editing by Aidan Lewis)

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua will draw the most lucrative gate in British boxing history says Dana White
articles.summary: Tickets for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's December 11 showdown went on sale on Friday ahead of their long-anticipated meeting at Cardiff's Principality Stadium; Dana White says it will draw the most lucrative gate in the history of British boxing
articles.body:
Tickets for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua's December 11 showdown at the Principality stadium in Cardiff went on sale on Friday, with the most expensive regular seats going for £13,128.

The Principality Stadium can hold more than 70,000 spectators and White revealed on Friday evening: "I think there's less than 700 tickets left. You can consider this thing a sellout already."

More than half a million people joined the Ticketmaster queue to snap up tickets for the long-awaited heavyweight bout on December 11, with thousands being sold within an hour of the launch.

"There were over 500,000 people in the queue. Incredible. But for our generation, two of the biggest, most famous heavyweights in boxing. And not even arguable it's the biggest UK fight ever between two British heavyweights," White told Sky Sports .

Before the sale commenced, Ticketmaster confirmed regular seats would cost between £88.50 and £13,128.

Those figures did not include VIP packages, hotel and travel packages, group or concession prices.

White anticipates the fight will draw the most lucrative gate in the history of British boxing. "Definitely. It will. I don't want to mis-speak here but we have this thing scaled for around $34 million," he said.

"The UK is the right place for this fight to happen but it will have done well anywhere."

The most expensive tickets exceed face-value figures for some of the world's biggest sporting events, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, where some seats were listed for £8,333.

In 2015 Floyd Mayweather's bout against Manny Pacquiao sold out within a minute , with top-priced face-value seats costing fans £4,982 .

Fury last fought in London in April against Arslanbek Makhmudov, where ringside seats at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium were priced at £3,000.

Comparatively, ringside tickets for his bout against Dillian Whyte at Wembley in 2022, were priced at £2,250.

The cheapest seats on the pitch for Fury vs Joshua were listed at £345, while others ranged from £700 to £900.

Some of the lowest-priced tickets in the stadium's upper terrace were on sale for £205.20. Ringside seats were also being sold on StubHub for more than £8,000.

Ringwalks are expected to commence at around 1am local time to cater for an international audience.

No rematch clause has been included in the contract for the fight, but that does not mean a second bout cannot be negotiated.

When the December 11 fight was made it was announced that Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and American combat sports promoter Dana White were staging the contest. However Eddie Hearn, who promotes Joshua, has publicly claimed the American cannot be involved.

White, renowned for creating the UFC, said of his role in this event: "Helped them with the gate, putting everything together. We're going to do all the production, produce the show and do what I do every Saturday."

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Dana White credits Eddie Hearn for Fury vs Joshua being in UK
articles.summary: Dana White gives credit to Eddie Hearn, but says he is "bored" of the ongoing feud between him and his rival promoter.
articles.body:
Dana White has credited Eddie Hearn for making sure the long-awaited fight between Tyson Fury and Antony Joshua will be held in the UK but insisted he was "bored" of their ongoing feud.

The heavyweight bout will take place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff - despite efforts to host it New York's Madison Square Garden - on a bill that starts on 11 December, though they are not expected to fight until the early hours of 12 December.

White and Saudi Arabian organisers wanted the bout in the United States, but Joshua and his promoter Hearn refused to budge on their contractual right to have it in the UK.

"You've got to give credit to Eddie for really grinding that and making sure that it happened in the UK," UFC president and Zuffa Boxing chief White told Steve Bunce on the 5 Live Boxing with Bunce podcast.

However, there had been doubts over the contest because of a dispute over the role of White in the promotion of the event.

The fight, which will be shown on Netflix, has been presented as a collaboration between Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and White.

Hearn has been publicly feuding with White since the launch of Zuffa Boxing earlier this year and said his involvement in the fight "ain't happening".

But, Fury and Joshua held a news conference on 30 September, to ease concerns over their fight.

White was not present at that media event but insisted "me and my team will be producing the fight that night".

"I guess we'll call me one of the promoters of the event because you do have Frank Warren (Fury's promoter) and Eddie Hearn that are both promoters too, promoting the event," he added.

Hearn has repeatedly said White could not promote the bout, but this week suggested he was prepared to meet the American to see how he could be involved.

White said that while he was willing to meet Hearn, he did not feel a sit-down was necessary.

"I'm actually bored with this now. Who cares? This isn't about me and Eddie Hearn," White said.

"It's about AJ and Fury. It's about this heavyweight fight.

"It's an Eddie show, not a Dana and Eddie show. It's boring now. This is about AJ and Fury.

"This was never the Dana and Eddie show. It's been all the Eddie show."

articles.title: Primeiros helicópteros enviados pelo governo federal para combater queimadas no AM chegam a Manaus | G1
articles.standfirst: Reforço ocorre em meio ao agravamento das queimadas no estado e após uma divergência entre o governo federal e o Corpo de Bombeiros do Amazonas sobre a oferta de apoio para enfrentar o fogo.
articles.summary: Reforço ocorre em meio ao agravamento das queimadas no estado e após uma divergência entre o governo federal e o Corpo de Bombeiros do Amazonas sobre a oferta de apoio para enfrentar o fogo.
articles.body:
Helicópteros enviados pelo governo federal para auxiliar combate à queimadas no AM pousaram no Aeroporto Internacional Eduardo Gomes, em Manaus. — Foto: Joel Araújo/Ibama

As primeiras aeronaves enviadas pelo governo federal para auxiliar no combate à queimadas florestais no Amazonas chegaram a Manaus no início da tarde deste sábado (10). Tratam-se de dois helicópteros do Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama) , que pousaram no Aeroporto Internacional Eduardo Gomes.

Os helicópteros fazem parte da frota de seis aeronaves que serão enviadas pelo Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA) para dar suporte no combate aos incêndios no estado, conforme anunciado pela pasta na quinta-feira (9).

Além dos dois helicópteros, outros quatro aviões modelo Air Tractor, usados no lançamento de água, devem pousar na capital amazonense neste sábado. A pasta também vai enviar 290 brigadistas.

Uma comitiva com a presença do ministro da Integração, Waldez Goés, e representantes dos ministérios do Meio Ambiente, Justiça e Segurança Pública, Saúde, além do presidente do Ibama, vem a Manaus ainda no sábado.

O grupo deve participar de uma reunião na sede da Superintendência da Zona Franca de Manaus (Suframa). No domingo, farão um sobrevoo em área de queimadas.

Bombeiros do Amazonas e governo federal divergem sobre ajuda

O reforço ocorre em meio ao agravamento das queimadas no estado e após uma divergência entre o governo federal e o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM) sobre a oferta de apoio para enfrentar o fogo.

A pasta informou que o objetivo é dar continuidade às ações de combate aos incêndios florestais no estado.

De acordo com o MMA, desde o início da temporada de incêndios, o Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama) extinguiu 229 incêndios no Amazonas e continua atuando no combate a outros 20 focos ativos .

A pasta não informou onde estão concentradas as operações. O governo federal também mantém operações de monitoramento e enfrentamento das queimadas.

O anúncio ocorreu horas após o comandante do CBMAM, coronel Orleilso Muniz, afirmar, nesta sexta-feira (9), que o governo federal negou um pedido de apoio para combater incêndios florestais no estado.

Em nota, o ministério contestou a declaração e informou que o governo amazonense havia solicitado ajuda em setembro, mas dispensou uma equipe federal antes de seu deslocamento para o campo.

A divergência veio à tona durante entrevista de Muniz ao Jornal do Amazonas 1ª Edição , da Rede Amazônica . Na ocasião, o comandante disse que a corporação havia solicitado aeronaves para combater incêndios, inclusive em áreas sob responsabilidade federal.

"Nós já tivemos um retorno negativo, de que não seria possível apoiar. Reforço e apelo mais uma vez: o estado do Amazonas precisa somar esforços com o Governo Federal para fazer um enfrentamento qualificado", afirmou.

Ao g1 , os bombeiros enviaram dois ofícios onde constam o pedido de recursos para auxiliar no combate aos incêndios florestais, solicitado ao Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, em 18 de setembro, e a resposta da pasta, assinado em 1º de outubro.

Em resposta, o Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública informou que não poderia atender à solicitação naquele momento. Segundo o documento, a Secretaria Nacional de Segurança Pública não dispunha de equipamentos desse tipo para doação e indicou alternativas para a obtenção de recursos federais.

No pedido, assinado por Muniz, é citado a necessidade de quatro aeronaves para combater o fogo, uma aeronave para transportar equipes e equipamentos e recursos para a compra ou aluguel de veículos.

Governo do AM solicitou e desistiu de ajuda, diz MMA

Segundo o MMA, em 23 de setembro, o Centro Integrado Multiagência de Coordenação Operacional Federal (Ciman Federal), coordenado pelo Ibama, recebeu uma solicitação de apoio do governo do Amazonas. Em resposta, foram acionados combatentes do Projeto de Resposta em Ações Integradas para Atuação em Situações de Desastres (Respad) e uma aeronave do Projeto de Gerenciamento de Aeronaves para Situações de Urgência e Socorro (Pegasus).

O ministério informou que, em 30 de setembro, após chuvas contribuírem para o controle dos focos de incêndio, o governo estadual comunicou que não precisava mais do apoio do Respad. Com isso, a equipe federal foi dispensada antes de se deslocar para atuar em campo.

A pasta também afirmou que orientou o governo estadual a solicitar recursos por meio do Sistema Nacional de Proteção e Defesa Civil (SINPDEC) para ampliar a capacidade de resposta aos incêndios. Até o momento, segundo o ministério, o pedido não foi formalizado.

Além das ações de combate, o governo federal informou que apoia o Amazonas por meio do projeto ProAmazon, financiado pelo Fundo Amazônia com R$ 45 milhões. Conforme o MMA, os pagamentos foram realizados em janeiro de 2025 e março de 2026, com recursos destinados ao fortalecimento da estrutura do Corpo de Bombeiros e às ações de prevenção e combate a incêndios florestais e queimadas não autorizadas.

Envio de reforço em meio ao agravamento do cenário

O anúncio do reforço para atuar no Amazonas ocorre em meio ao agravamento do cenário no estado. Neste sábado, a fumaça voltou a encobrir Manaus pelo terceiro dia consecutivo, e a concentração de partículas chegou a 209,1 µg/m³ em um dos pontos monitorados na capital amazonense.

O índice supera em 736,4% o limite de 25 µg/m³ usado pelo Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental (Selva), da Universidade do Estado do Amazonas (UEA), para classificar a qualidade do ar como boa.

Por volta das 6h, o sensor instalado na Secretaria de Estado do Meio Ambiente (Sema), na Zona Centro-Sul, registrava 209,1 µg/m³, nível classificado como péssimo. Na região central da cidade, a concentração chegou a 164,1 µg/m³, enquanto o sensor no Morro da Liberdade marcou 157,2 µg/m³. Os três pontos apresentavam qualidade do ar considerada péssima.

Falta de chuvas agrava incêndios no Amazonas; fumaça já afeta mais de 20 cidades, incluindo a capital — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

articles.body:
Bombeiros atuam em incêndio em zona rural de Itacoatiara. — Foto: Liam Cavalcante/Rede Amazônica

O governo do Amazonas solicitou apoio do governo federal para combater queimadas florestais, mas dispensou uma equipe de brigadistas antes que ela se deslocasse para atuar no estado, informou o Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA). Neste sábado (10), as primeiras aeronaves enviadas pela União chegaram a Manaus . Uma comitiva federal também deve chegar à capital durante a noite para acompanhar as ações.

Ajuda foi dispensada após chuvas, diz ministério

O Ministério do Meio Ambiente informou que recebeu, em 23 de setembro, uma solicitação de apoio do governo do Amazonas por meio do Centro Integrado Multiagência de Coordenação Operacional Federal (Ciman Federal), coordenado pelo Ibama, para o reforço das ações de combate aos incêndios florestais nos municípios de Novo Aripuanã, Careiro da Várzea, Autazes, Manaquiri, Urucurituba, Apuí, Manicoré, Manacapuru e Caapiranga.

O MMA afirmou ainda que orientou o governo estadual a solicitar recursos pelo Sistema Nacional de Proteção e Defesa Civil (SINPDEC) para ampliar a capacidade de resposta aos incêndios. Até este sábado, segundo a pasta, o pedido não havia sido formalizado.

O g1 questionou o governo do Amazonas se a dispensa da equipe federal em 30 de setembro foi uma decisão formal do estado e qual o posicionamento sobre a divergência, mas até a publicação desta reportagem não obteve resposta.

Bombeiros dizem que pedido de aeronaves foi negado

A declaração do comandante dos bombeiros que deu início à divergência ocorreu na sexta-feira (9). Durante entrevista à Rede Amazônica, Orleilso Muniz afirmou que a corporação havia recebido uma resposta negativa ao pedido de apoio federal.

No documento, o Ministério da Justiça informou que não poderia atender à solicitação naquele momento. Segundo a resposta, a Secretaria Nacional de Segurança Pública não dispunha de equipamentos daquele tipo para doação e indicou alternativas para a obtenção de recursos federais.

O pedido, assinado por Muniz, previa quatro aeronaves para combater o fogo, uma aeronave para transportar equipes e equipamentos e recursos para a compra ou o aluguel de veículos.

Além da mobilização de equipes e aeronaves, o Ministério do Meio Ambiente afirmou que o governo federal apoia o Amazonas por meio do projeto ProAmazon, financiado pelo Fundo Amazônia com R$ 45 milhões.

O ministério também informou que, desde o início da temporada de incêndios, o Ibama extinguiu 229 incêndios no Amazonas e continua atuando no combate a outros 20 focos ativos. A pasta não informou onde as operações estão concentradas.

articles.title: Dricus Du Plessis believes he could fight for the title next
articles.summary: Former middleweight champion Dricus Du Plessis believes he could find himself fighting for the title next.
articles.body:
Former middleweight champion Dricus Du Plessis captured the 185-pound title at UFC 297 in January 2024 by defeating current titleholder Sean Strickland via spit decision. He dominated Strickland in their rematch at UFC 312 .

"Stillknocks" lost the belt to Khamzat Chimaev in one-sided fashion at UFC 319 but rebounded from the loss in his last outing by soundly defeating former welterweight champion Kamaru Usman . With the win, and considering the landscape in the weight class, Du Plessis believes he could fight for the title next.

"After the last fight, I just prove again that I can be the best in the world and that I will be the best in the world. Where we are at right now is continuing building on those blocks that we built before that fight. Looking at what's next, I mean, time waits for no one. Right now, they're obviously going to do Strickland and [Nassourdine] Imavov . I think the middleweight division is in a bit of a, it's a weird situation because who gets the next title shot? And I'm 100% ready for that," Du Plessis told Fight Forecast .

In light of Strickland's recent comments about wanting to transition into boxing and a willingness to give up the 185-pound title, the top of the middleweight division is at a standstill. Strickland wants more money and judging from his social media posts, negotiations aren't going well.

"I had an injury. I was out for a while, but I told them I would be ready to fight early next year. It's interesting because I don't know what they're going to do. Who are they going to make me fight? They're not going to make me fight backwards. And right now we have Strickland, Imavov, Khamzat and myself. So, It's going to be interesting," continued the South African.

"You're as good as your last fight. Obviously I last a bout. I was off 11 months working on everything to be the best in the world again. I have no doubt that I will be champion again."

articles.title: Joey Essex warms up for Dapper Laughs fight
articles.summary: The reality TV star trains with his uncle, Tony Sims, and has a large boxing family.
articles.body:
Three years ago, Joey Essex tried to manifest his dream of continuing his family boxing heritage by writing his own homemade contract.

The 36-year-old had already found fame through ITV's The Only Way is Essex and had travelled the world for Channel 4's Educating Joey Essex.

But climbing into the ring was the new ambition, which he fulfilled in August 2025 when he fought Portuguese influencer Joao Barbosa.

Essex returns to screens when he faces comedian Daniel O'Reilly, aka Dapper Laughs, on Saturday evening for his second fight.

Essex, from Chigwell, dreamt of joining the Misfits sports promotion company when he wrote himself the contract one morning in 2023.

"Did I write that I was going to be headlining a show? No, I didn't write that. So I've actually gone past my dreams," he told the BBC.

"My family are quite huge in boxing, it kind of stems in my blood. So kind of makes sense for me, with my name, to be involved."

Donny, his father, fought more than a dozen times under the Amateur Boxing Alliance without going professional.

Meanwhile, his uncle and trainer Tony Sims has guided big names including Anthony Joshua and Ricky Burns.

Sims initially told Essex he "should never be a boxer" because he was "too pretty", but his nephew has become his latest project at his gym in Stapleford Abbotts.

Essex insisted he was not trying to turn professional, but added: "I feel like if I didn't ever do this, I would have always thought 'what if?'"

Essex beat Barbosa, also known as Numeiro, by a points decision, but described the contest as "a slugfest".

He hopes Saturday evening in Bermondsey, south London, will be a better spectacle.

"Let's hope there's actually some boxing involved," he said.

He wants to fight the bigger names at Misfits, such as online influencers KSI, Logan Paul and boxer Tommy Fury.

"People can believe in you, but you need to believe in yourself," he finished.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua undercard: Jai Opetaia could fight Deontay Wilder on Principality Stadium bill
articles.summary: Former heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder and cruiserweight star Jai Opetaia look set to collide on the undercard of the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua all-British mega-fight on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff; Opetaia's long-term target remains David Benavidez
articles.body:
Fury and Joshua meet in a long-awaited, much-anticipated all-British heavyweight fight at the Principality Stadium.

Wilder, the hard-punching former world heavyweight champion, is eyeing a place on the bill against elite cruiserweight Jai Opetaia.

Dana White, who promotes Opetaia, told Sky Sports : "Jai Opetaia is more than likely going to be on the undercard. [Wilder] is one that we've been talking about and working on."

It would be a first high-level heavyweight fight for Opetaia, the unbeaten Australian who has been a force at cruiserweight.

Wilder is now 40 years old but the former WBC titlist is still known for his fearsome punch-power.

"The guy's willing to fight anybody," White said of Opetaia. "It's a very dangerous fight for him considering where he sits in his division right now.

"But he's a fighter; he'll fight anybody, even at heavyweight with a guy who hits as hard as Wilder does."

Opetaia would likely return to cruiserweight afterwards. He and David Benavidez are considered the two best fighters in the 200lb weight class and Benavidez remains Opetaia's ultimate target.

"That's the fight he really wants. He wants that fight so we've got to figure that one out," White said, adding: "He wants to stay active, he wants to fight and he doesn't care if it's at heavyweight or wherever, he's ready to go."

Wilder had an epic trilogy with Tyson Fury and came close to setting a fight with Anthony Joshua, only to lose to Joseph Parker.

In his last fight Wilder battled to a points win over British contender Derek Chisora at The O2 in London in April.

articles.title: Lewis Crocker: Former IBF welterweight champion plots his route back to the top
articles.summary: Lewis Crocker is looking forward and not back at his world title defeat by Liam Paro as he prepares for his return against Owen Cooper in December at Belfast's 02.
articles.body:
The flight home from Australia in June was a little longer for Lewis Crocker as he pondered his defeat by Liam Paro in his first defence of the IBF welterweight title.

A storming finish by the Belfast man was not enough to turn things around as all three judges gave Paro a 115-113 decision and the Australian realised his dream of becoming a two-weight champion.

Crocker grew into that fight and seemed on the brink of finding a finish in the late rounds, but Paro held on and Crocker lost his grip on the title he won last September in Belfast's Windsor Park against Paddy Donovan - his record slipping to 22 wins with one loss.

"Shoulda, woulda, coulda," is how the 29-year-old reflects on that night in Brisbane - one in which he was so near yet so far away, yet his first career defeat has not dented confidence, but only served to fuel his desire to rise again.

"I got beaten on a very close decision in a world title fight against a two-weight world champion," Crocker told BBC Sport NI.

"I gained experience from it anyway, and at 29 I've still got plenty more for whatever opportunity is coming.

"I felt like I had him hurt a lot of times and he was holding, if he gets a point taken off then I win the fight. Shoulda, woulda, coulda...

"That was a long fight back, but I'm over it because I know I'm right there. My main focus now is going to be a two-time world champion."

The first step on that quest takes place at The O2 in Belfast on 19 December when Crocker faces former English champion Owen Cooper [12-2] on the undercard of the Anthony Cacace v Nick Ball world super-featherweight title clash.

Perhaps it's further evidence that the old promotional cold war in British boxing is over as Crocker - promoted by Matchroom - will box on a Queensberry card and he is delighted to be back on home turf, promising fans a "Christmas Crocker" on the night.

That his first world title defence didn't take place in his home city instead of over 10,000 miles away on the east coast of Australia could be a source of consternation.

However, Crocker has always held a philosophical view of it all, insisting the opportunity to defend a world title in Australia is "something you'd dream of as a kid".

Still, it is good to be home as he embarks upon a route back to the top and while opportunities may present themselves in 2027, Crocker is not looking past the challenge of 26-year-old Cooper who will see this as his golden ticket.

"It would have been great to have a first defence in Belfast, but ultimately it doesn't matter - there's still two men getting into the ring," Crocker reasoned.

"It's good to be back in Belfast anyway, and get on the road to two-time world champion.

"More than anything now, I want to be a two-time world champion and we've a great plan ahead but I'm not looking past Owen, because he's a great fighter and I'm expecting a really tough test."

Crocker's old foe Paddy Donovan is front of the queue to face Paro, while the welterweight division has come alive once again with some of the sport's biggest names in Ryan Garcia [WBC], Teofimo Lopez [WBA] and Devin Haney [WBO] holding the other titles.

A second shot at a title at Windsor Park where he won his first against Donovan "would be great" but whomever and wherever, Crocker would be happy to take.

"There are four world titles out there, so any one of them [would be great]," he continued.

"[I plan to get] back on track and push towards it, but as I say, Owen's my main focus right now."

articles.title: Three wins down, a title shot to chase: Brendan Allen's next test is Christian Leroy Duncan
articles.summary: Brendan Allen wanted a fight higher up the UFC middleweight rankings.
articles.body: Brendan Allen wanted a fight higher up the UFC middleweight rankings. Instead, he will put his own position on the line against Christian Leroy Duncan, a rising contender who has won five consecutive fights.Allen, ranked No. 4 in the division, has won his last three bouts, most recently beating Edmen Shahbazyan by unanimous decision on June 6. Duncan, ranked No. 10, heads into his first UFC main event on the back of consecutive decision wins over Roman Dolidze and former title challenger Jared Cannonier.For Allen, the fight is another chance to keep moving in a division where he believes he should be facing opponents above him. It also comes as he continues to look towards a possible matchup with former middleweight champion Dricus du Plessis.Allen has maintained that a fight with Du Plessis had effectively been agreed earlier this year before it fell through. He was left looking for another opponent, eventually taking on Shahbazyan. Du Plessis, meanwhile, went on to face Kamaru Usman and won by unanimous decision.Asked whether he still believed the Du Plessis fight had been avoided, Allen did not hold back.“Yeah, 100% I believe the fight was avoided. I think Dricus ducked me,” he said.“I understand the name value of the guy he fought (Kamaru Usman), but in terms of competition level, like where we're at today, I think it was a lot different. I know I'm a way harder fight than Usman, especially with all the circumstances, age and coming up a weight class. I know it in my heart. He knows it in his heart. He took the easier fight,” Allen told TimesofIndia.com.That remains a matchup Allen wants, but he has not been willing to wait indefinitely for it to happen. His approach has been to keep fighting, even when the opponent on offer does not necessarily move him up the rankings.“I don't say this fight's the right fight for me. It's just the only fight available, and I want to stay active and make money while I can,” he said of Duncan.“So, I think fighting up is the right fight, but it didn't happen, and I can't sit back and ponder on it or complain. I've just got to go out there and do my best and try to get the W, and then fight up after that.”Allen said the uncertainty around the division was only a small part of why he wanted to remain active. He also wants to keep improving and earn while he can.“Not trusting the division to move is definitely one reason, but that one's very minimal. I just don't want to sit out. I want to make money. I spend money like crazy, so I've got to make it. I've got to hustle and just keep staying active. Also, it helps my body stay good and keeps me growing, keeps me doing what I need to do. And yeah, I just want to fight, I want to stay active.”The middleweight pictureThe division is not short of contenders making a case for themselves. Sean Strickland holds the title, while Khamzat Chimaev, Du Plessis and Nassourdine Imavov are among the names ahead of Allen in the middleweight rankings.That leaves Allen with ground to make up, even after three successive wins. Duncan's rise adds another complication. A victory over the fourth-ranked fighter would be the biggest result of his UFC career and could move him into contention for fights against the division's leading names.Allen, meanwhile, knows that another win does not automatically guarantee a title opportunity. He was candid when asked when a fighter should stop accepting bouts and start demanding a shot at the belt.“Winning fights is always the biggest thing, but I think in this company, you don't demand a damn thing. You go out there and earn it, and no matter if you keep fighting and keep winning, you never demand anything. You just keep pushing for it, keep trying, and when you've earned your shot, you can sit out and wait if you want to.”He does not believe he has reached that point yet.“So I just haven't earned mine yet, given the state of the division and how it's been going and who's been available. But hopefully, this one or one more, I can say I owned it and can sit and wait.”For Allen, beating Duncan could strengthen his argument for a fight against someone higher in the rankings. He also has a specific idea of what would put him in a stronger position to challenge for the belt.“If I beat Duncan on Saturday, I think I either fight Dricus if he stops ducking me, or sit and wait for the belt. But I think Dricus is more realistic. If I beat Leroy and then go out and beat Dricus, then I can sit and wait, because then there's nobody for sure over me to get the title shot.”Keeping the focus on himselfAllen's recent camps have taken him to Chicago, where he has worked with Mike Valle and Belal Muhammad. He said the main benefit has been the attention he receives during preparation and the chance to concentrate on his own development.“The environment's been good, but ultimately, it's just been having one-on-one attention and being focused solely on myself during my camps on how I can get better and prepare for the guy that I'm fighting, rather than being in a big room and having so many eyes on me all over the place.”The knee issue he spoke about after his win over Shahbazyan has also been addressed. Allen said rehabilitation had gone well and that it had not affected his preparation for Duncan.“The knee is good. My knee didn't affect anything. I did a lot of rehab, and it's good to go.”There is also the time away from his family that comes with training camps and travel. Allen said managing that side of his career has become more difficult than the physical demands of fighting.“Definitely managing everything around camp and my family and being away from them and not seeing them that much and traveling like for this and for that for camps — and that's one million percent the harder scenario. That's the harder thing to deal with, for sure.”Allen's immediate focus is Duncan, not the fight he believes should have happened earlier in the year. articles.title: Masvidal se pone del lado de Topuria: "Ese tío es un luchador nato"
articles.standfirst: El ex peleador de la UFC defendió a 'El Matador' y su coraje a pesar de su derrota en el UFC Casa Blanca
articles.summary: El ex peleador de la UFC defendió a 'El Matador' y su coraje a pesar de su derrota en el UFC Casa Blanca
articles.body: Jorge Masvidal conoce bien a Ilia Topuria, ya que estuvieron entrenando juntos en el 'Climent Club' cuando 'El Matador' todavía residía en Alicante. El peleador estadounidense ha hablado al respecto de las críticas que ha recibido el peleador hispanogeorgiano después de que su esquina parase su combate ante Justin Gaethje en el UFC Casa Blanca, saliendo en su defensa y remarcando la gran valentía de Ilia. El pasado 14 de junio, Topuria perdió el invicto y el cinturón de peso ligero en la Casa Blanca ante un Gaethje que realizó el combate de su vida para cumplir su sueño de ser campeón indiscutido. Al finalizar el cuarto asalto Ilia ya tenía la nariz y los dos orbitales rotos, por lo que su hermano Aleksandre decidió parar la pelea. Sin embargo, Masvidal ha dejado claro de qué pasta está hecho 'El Matador'. "Detuvieron el combate y él no protestó, pero vaya, tiene los dos ojos cerrados y la nariz rota. No intento compadecerme de él, simplemente expongo los hechos: ese tipo es una bestia. Está dispuesto a morir ahí dentro. Resulta que posee las habilidades adecuadas; está dotado genéticamente de velocidad y potencia. Así que creo que aprendió que, por muchos dones que tengas, no dejas de ser humano", afirmó en una entrevista con 'Full Mount MMA'. Después de esa derrota, Topuria se tomó un par de meses de descanso alejado del foco mediático para sanar tanto física como mentalmente, y a principios de septiembre reapareció con un ensayo donde definía lo que había supuesto para él esa derrota y cómo pensaba volver más fuerte. Vivió por primera vez la cara B de la moneda en su carrera profesional pero, como él dijo, no era la primera vez que perdía en esta vida. Ahora su misión es prepararse lo mejor posible para su siguiente reto, que todavía está en el aire. Las dos opciones que parecen más viables son la revancha con Justin Gaethje o un supercombate ante Paddy Pimblett, y ambos casos serán una prueba de fuego para un Topuria que tendrá que vivir por primera vez lo que supone tener que demostrar su valía después de caer derrotado. Las grandes leyendas no se forjan en las victorias, sino en momentos como el que está viviendo ahora mismo 'El Matador', y Masvidal tiene claro que este traspiés no cambiará su talento ni su destino en las MMA, que es ser uno de los mejores peleadores de todos los tiempos.

articles.title: Mike Tyson predicts ‘Donald Trump will win’ midterms before joining president for New York rally
articles.summary: Mike Tyson visited the White House and predicted a Trump midterm elections victory before joining the president at a rally in Syracuse, New York.
articles.body: Boxing legend Mike Tyson is backing President Donald Trump’s political corner ahead of November’s midterm elections. The former heavyweight champion visited the White House on Friday and offered a brief prediction when reporters asked how Republicans would fare in the midterms. "I believe Donald Trump is gonna win it," Tyson said at the West Wing briefing room before accompanying the president to a rally in Syracuse, New York. TRUMP RALLIES NEW YORK CROWD FOR REPUBLICAN BRUCE BLAKEMAN'S BID TO REPLACE GOV. KATHY HOCHUL Before their departure, Trump joked about standing alongside one of boxing’s most feared fighters. "I won’t be fighting him today," Trump told reporters, adding, "We’ve been friends for a long time." TRUMP BRINGS MIKE TYSON ON STAGE AT SYRACUSE RALLY, JOKES THAT HE IS BRUCE BLAKEMAN'S PERSONAL SECURITY Their relationship dates to the 1980s, when Trump hosted boxing events featuring Tyson in Atlantic City. Their connection has since extended into cannabis advocacy. Tyson’s cannabis advocacy has become another connection in his decades-long friendship with Trump. In June 2025, Tyson joined Kevin Durant and other athletes in urging the White House to pursue federal marijuana reform. Their requests extended beyond rescheduling: They sought clemency for nonviolent marijuana offenses and changes to banking restrictions affecting cannabis businesses. Tyson told Fox News Digital rescheduling was his top priority, expressing disappointment with former Presidents Barack Obama and Joe Biden’s handling of cannabis reform.. "It was a letdown, but you have to respect they were in power. You have to respect that," Tyson said. "We have a different president now, so we're talking to him. So, it seems to be a lot different talking to President Trump than with the other guy. And, like I said before, that's their agenda. This is our agenda right here." Tyson added he believes the rescheduling of marijuana is the top priority in his federal reform goals. On top of that, he and his supporters want to see mass clemency for nonviolent marijuana offenders. Trump took a step toward that goal in December 2025, signing an executive order directing the attorney general to expedite marijuana’s proposed move from Schedule I to Schedule III. The order instructed officials to complete the federal rulemaking process; it did not itself finalize the change. Tyson welcomed the order while urging Trump to go further. articles.title: Boxing: Former UFC fighter Michael 'Venom' Page signs with Misfits boxing
articles.summary: Former UFC fighter Michael 'Venom' Page says he is "coming to show the boxing world what I can do".
articles.body:
Former UFC fighter Michael 'Venom' Page says he is "coming to show the boxing world what I can do" after joining the Misfits promotion outfit.

The 39-year-old's last fight on his UFC contract took place in September when he beat Nursulton Ruziboev to register a fifth win in six fights since making his debut for the organisation in 2024.

Despite his record in the UFC, Page, known as MVP, was dropped by the MMA promotion and is linking up with Misfits Boxing.

The Londoner has signed a "multi-fight, multi-year agreement".

"I've been in combat sports for a long time and I've had plenty of options, but MF Sports is the right fit for me," said Page.

"They're doing things differently, the energy is huge, and the fights are big.

"I'm excited for this new chapter, and I'm coming to show the boxing world what I can do. I feel free, shackles are off."

Page has won 26 of his 29 MMA fights and is a decorated kickboxer.

The former Bellator star made his professional boxing debut in 2017 and is 2-0, but has not boxed since 2018.

KSI, a co-founder of Misfits, announced MVP's arrival at an event on Saturday.

"Michael Venom Page is one of the biggest names in combat sports, and everyone wanted him," said the influencer, musician and former boxer.

"For him to choose Misfits says everything about where we are as a promotion. He's a superstar, he's explosive, and fans are going to love watching him in the ring with us."

Francisco Prado snapped his four-fight losing skid in a big way – against a big opponent – at UFC Fight Night 290 .

Prado, who was moving down from welterweight, gladly accepted and decided to return the favor by packing on a whopping 35 pounds just 24 hours after weigh ins.
